livescore_last_success.decays: the key lives 7 days after its last write, and every Live Score error rewrites it; the first success after access returns overwrites last_success_at. From then on the repair refuses: --apply takes the cut only from --livescore-last-success (2026-10-02T14:53:28.028159Z), and refuses when Redis records any other last success, because the outage the plan was made for has ended and the plan has to be made again by a person

backend_guard.what_it_shows: Why the --apply guard cannot rest on pg_stat_activity. In development the backend's engine uses NullPool (app/db/session.py), so it holds no database connection between passes. At this read the backend (pid 38897, started 2026-10-07T02:51:55Z by another session) was listening on 127.0.0.1:8000 and its scheduler had written settle 8 s earlier, yet pg_stat_activity listed 0 other clients on soccer_predictions. The script now refuses the backend's database without --i-stopped-the-backend whatever pg_stat_activity shows, and checks the claim: the address, the sync locks, the last two ticks, and again just before COMMIT.
backend_guard.backend_address_127.0.0.1:8000: accepts connections (a TCP connection opened and closed; no request sent)
refusals_the_script_gives_on_this_state: with --owner-approved and without --i-stopped-the-backend: refusing to write to soccer_predictions, the database the backend uses, without --i-stopped-the-backend ... An empty pg_stat_activity proves nothing

with --owner-approved and --i-stopped-the-backend: refusing to write to soccer_predictions while the backend looks alive, whatever --i-stopped-the-backend says: 127.0.0.1:8000 accepts connections; the scheduler recorded sync:task:settle 8 s ago (less than two ticks)
